findings.title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false, making the feature flag dead code
findings.body: The function computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` but then returns false both when `enabled` is true and when it is false. As written, `FlagSqlExpressions` has no effect and the SQL expression path can never be re-enabled through the existing feature toggle. If the security fix is intended to hard-disable SQL expressions, this should be an explicit unconditional `return false` with no feature-toggle call; if the flag is meant to remain usable later, the logic is wrong. The current code is misleading and likely to cause an accidental revert or bad future re-enablement.

findings.title: No tests cover the SQL expression disable behavior
findings.body: This PR closes a critical RCE/LFI path by rejecting QueryTypeSQL in the reader and by replacing DuckDB with a not-implemented stub, but no tests are added. There should be regression tests asserting that SQL expression queries are rejected both through ReadQuery and through NewSQLCommand/UnmarshalSQLCommand, so a future change that restores execution or unintentionally weakens the guard is caught. Without such tests, the security fix is only protected by the current stub implementation and not by the test suite.
